rules.route: Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals

note: Hong Kong keeps its own immigration control. A performer needs (a Macao resident too, whose passport is China's nationality but who is no resident of Hong Kong) an employment visa or entry permit from the Immigration Department, a Mainland resident through the Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (including one-off project-based work). Under the STV Scheme, a talent invited by an organisation authorised for the arts and cultural sector may perform as a visitor, paid, for up to 14 consecutive days each trip without one (LegCo reply, 15 October 2025); modelled as 14 days, the invitation being the host's to give.

sources.title: Hong Kong Government, LCQ16: Measures to facilitate entry of performing groups into Hong Kong (15 October 2025)
sources.said: Eligible Mainland residents who possess special skills, knowledge or experience of value to and not readily available in Hong Kong may apply to come to work in Hong Kong under the Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP) ... including short-term or one-off project-based employment, if the conditions are met. ... Invited persons may come to Hong Kong to participate in specified short-term activities as visitors without the need to apply for employment visas/entry permits from the ImmD. They may participate in specified short-term activities for up to 14 consecutive calendar days during each trip to Hong Kong, and receive remuneration for the specified activities concerned.
